'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**The [[Israel Defense Forces]] carry out airstrikes on [[Khan Yunis]] and [[Gaza City]] in the [[Gaza Strip]] in the early morning, in response to [[incendiary balloon]]s being flown from Gaza, putting the ceasefire in jeopardy. This comes after the [[Dance of Flags]] march was held in [[East Jerusalem]]. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/israel-palestine-gaza-air-strikes-fragile-ceasefire-jeopardy (Middle East Eye)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/idf-strikes-gaza-terror-targets-after-arson-attacks-in-1st-raids-since-ceasefire (''Times of Israel'')]
**Mediators renew their push for another ceasefire between [[Israel]] and [[Hamas]] following the airstrikes. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/06/16/world/middleeast/israel-hamas-gaza-cease-fire.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the arts and cultural heritage]]
**The [[Taj Mahal]] reopens to tourists after a two-month closure due to the second wave of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in India|pandemic]] in [[India]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/taj-mahal-reopens-today-after-2-months-check-guidelines-for-tourists-101623818415856.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
*The [[United States House of Representatives]] votes 415–14 to make [[Juneteenth]] a federal holiday. This comes after the [[United States Senate]] voted unanimously to pass the same bill yesterday. The legislation will now head to [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] for his signature. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/house-passes-bill-make-juneteenth-federal-holiday-n1271083 (NBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra]]
****The Andorran government lifts the obligation to wear masks outdoors, at work meetings and with people who are immunized. [https://www.diariandorra.ad/noticies/nacional/2021/06/16/sense_mascareta_carrer_181912_1125.html (''Diari d'Andorra'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Macedonia]]
****[[North Macedonia]] lifts their nighttime curfew and allows outdoor organized events, weddings and concerts to be held at 50% capacity. The [[Government of North Macedonia|government]] also lifts working hour restrictions on the hospitality sector, betting shops, gas stations, and casinos. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/europe/2021-06/16/c_1310011601.htm (Xinhuanet)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 9,055 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total since February 25. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-uk-reports-9-055-new-cases-the-highest-daily-total-since-february-and-another-nine-deaths-12334084 (Sky News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]] surpasses 40,000 cases of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.khmertimeskh.com/50875439/grim-milestone-as-cambodia-passes-40000-case-mark/ (''Khmer Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maldives]]
****[[Maldives]] surpasses 200 deaths from COVID-19. [https://raajje.mv/101894 (Raajje)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] reports a record 2,395 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 83,128. [https://m.akipress.com/news:659453:Mongolia_recorded_2,395_new_cases_of_coronavirus,_9_deaths/ (AKI Press)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The [[United States]] [[Federal government of the United States|government]] purchases 200 million doses of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] produced by [[Moderna]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/us/articles/2021-06-16/us-buys-another-200-million-doses-of-modernas-covid-19-vaccine (U.S. News & World Report)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
****[[Royal Caribbean International]] announces that it is delaying the inaugural sailing of their brand-new ''[[Odyssey of the Seas]]'' [[cruise liner]] from [[Fort Lauderdale]] to July 31 after eight crew members tested positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/royal-caribbean-ceo-says-crew-members-odyssey-seas-test-positive-2021-06-16/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***[[South Africa]] restricts gatherings to 50 people for indoor social and religious events and 100 people for outdoor events, and also extends their curfew from 10:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. and restrict the sale of alcohol to Monday to Thursday from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases and hospitalizations. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/16/south-africa-increases-coronavirus-restrictions-as-cases-surge (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Botswana]]n mining company [[Debswana]] presents a 1,098-[[Carat (mass)|carat]] [[diamond]] discovered on June 1 to President [[Mokgweetsi Masisi]]. The company claims that it is the third-largest diamond ever discovered. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/jun/16/worlds-third-largest-diamond-discovered-in-botswana (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 Russia–United States summit]], [[Russia–United States relations]]
** U.S. President Joe Biden meets with [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] during a summit meeting in [[Geneva]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/biden-putin-geneva-summit-2021-06-16/ (CBS News)]
*[[Federal Ministry of Defence (Germany)|German Defence Minister]] [[Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer]] withdraws a [[platoon]] from a [[NATO]] mission in [[Lithuania]]. The withdrawal follows a report from ''[[Der Spiegel]]'' on Monday stating that the platoon's members engaged in misconduct, including [[bullying in the military|bullying]], filming a [[sexual assault]] against another soldier, and singing [[antisemitic]] songs to mark the birthday of dictator [[Adolf Hitler]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-57487869 (BBC News)]
*The [[Ethiopia]]n Foreign Ministry rejects an [[Arab League]] resolution calling for the [[United Nations Security Council|UN Security Council]] to intervene in the dispute over the [[Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam]] on behalf of [[Egypt]] and [[Sudan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/16/ethiopia-rejects-arab-league-resolution-on-renaissance-dam (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Fatou Bensouda]] steps down as [[Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court|Chief Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court]], a position she has held since 2012. She is succeeded by [[Karim Ahmad Khan]]. [https://m.jpost.com/israel-news/icc-prosecutor-to-step-down-tomorrow-new-chief-to-decide-israels-fate-671116/amp?__twitter_impression=true (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*At least sixty [[Berlin]] police officers are injured after [[Squatting|squatters]] in a [[Friedrichshain]] building attacked them with stones while conducting a fire inspection. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-57495064 (BBC News)]
